checks.why: a handler's route is its type's @RequestMapping prefix and its own mapping, and it is joined only to the requests that send its HTTP method: the three GETs of /orders drive list, the two POSTs do not

near miss: the same path under the other verb reaches the other handler, and five tests writing one path are not refused as a key that identifies nothing, since each handler is written by fewer than the cap
a relative method path joins the type's prefix: @PostMapping("lines") under /orders serves /orders/lines
